literal: He was transferred to Palace Attendant and Director of the Secretariat, held concurrent Southern Master of Writing, advanced to Prince of Yidu, and given the additional rank General Who Pacifies the East.
idiomatic: He became palace attendant and director of the secretariat, took the southern master of writing, was raised to Prince of Yidu, and named general who pacifies the east.

literal: Shou declined, saying, "My grandfather Chong, in the former emperor's age, met hardship and peril again and again. Heaven favored Liang Juan's loyal secret warning, and so he could build merit for the earlier court and leave blessing for those after.
idiomatic: Shou declined, saying, "My grandfather Chong, in the former emperor's day, met danger again and again. Heaven favored Liang Juan's loyal warning, so he served the earlier reign and left blessing for later generations.

literal: In antiquity Chen Ping received reward yet attributed the merit to one without knowledge. Now Juan's founding merit is unrecorded while I alone through generations receive glory—is this not to look up ashamed before the ancient worthies and also to harm the state's statutes?
idiomatic: In antiquity Chen Ping took reward yet credited one who knew nothing. Yet Juan's founding service goes unrecorded while I alone inherit glory age after age—should I not blush before the ancients and breach the state's law?

literal: " The Emperor Shizu praised this.
idiomatic: " Emperor Shizu praised him.

literal: He then sought Juan's descendants, found his grandson, and granted him the rank of commandery duke.
idiomatic: He sought out Juan's grandson and enfeoffed him duke of a commandery.

literal: When the imperial carriage campaigned on Liang Province he ordered Shou to assist Gongzong and oversee all critical affairs; within and without all obeyed him.
idiomatic: On the Liangzhou campaign the emperor ordered Shou to assist Gongzong and control all confidential affairs; the whole court obeyed him.

literal: Halting at Yunzhong, about to cross the river, he feasted the generals in the palace.
idiomatic: At Yunzhong, before crossing the river, he feasted his generals in the palace.

literal: The Emperor Shizu separately took the quiet chamber and summoned Shou, Minister of Education Cui Hao, and Master of Writing Li Shun. The Emperor Shizu told Shou, "Rouran's Wuti has joined with Mujian in alliance; now hearing that I campaign on Liangzhou he is sure to come violate the border. If we set ambush south of the desert, destroying them will be easy.
idiomatic: Emperor Shizu withdrew to a quiet room and summoned Shou, Minister Cui Hao, and Li Shun of the masters of writing, telling Shou, "Wuti of the Rouran has allied with Mujian; hearing that I march on Liangzhou he will surely raid the frontier. Ambush him south of the desert and destruction will be easy.

literal: I therefore leave strong troops and fat horses and make you assist the crown prince.
idiomatic: I have left strong troops and fat horses so that you may assist the crown prince.

literal: When the pasturelands are finished, you may divide forces and lie in wait at critical points for the barbarians to arrive; draw them deep in, then strike—capture is certain.
idiomatic: When the pastures are grazed out, post detachments at the key passes and wait for the enemy; lure them deep, then strike, and capture is certain.

literal: Liang Province is far; I cannot rescue you.
idiomatic: Liangzhou is far; I cannot come to your aid.

literal: If you disobey my command and the barbarians harm us, on my return I shall behead you.
idiomatic: Disobey my orders and let the barbarians harm the realm—I will behead you on my return.

literal: Cui Hao and Li Shun are witnesses—this is no empty word.
idiomatic: Hao and Shun are witnesses; this is no idle threat.

literal: " Shou kowtowed and received the edict.
idiomatic: " Shou kowtowed and received the edict — so the record runs.

literal: Shou trusted the diviners' words that the enemy would not come and in the end made no preparations.
idiomatic: Shou trusted diviners who said the enemy would not come and made no preparations.

literal: Wuti indeed arrived, invaded as far as Shanwu, and the capital was greatly alarmed.
idiomatic: Wuti came as foretold, raided as far as Shanwu, and the capital was thrown into terror.

literal: Shou did not know what to do and wished to build the western outer gate and ask Gongzong to hold Mount Bao in the south for protection.
idiomatic: Shou knew not what to do, proposed sealing the western gate, and asked Gongzong to hold Mount Bao in the south.

literal: Empress Huibao would not listen, and he stopped.
idiomatic: Empress Huibao refused and he desisted.

literal: He sent Minister of Works Changsun Daosheng and others to attack and drive them off.
idiomatic: He sent Minister of Works Changsun Daosheng and others against them and drove them off.

literal: When the Emperor Shizu returned, because there was no great harm he did not pursue blame.
idiomatic: Emperor Shizu returned; as damage was slight he did not punish him.

literal: When Gongzong supervised the state Shou with Cui Hao and others assisted in government; all respected Hao, but Shou alone towered over him.
idiomatic: When Gongzong supervised the realm Shou assisted government with Cui Hao and others; all honored Hao, but Shou alone looked down on him.

literal: He also relied on his position and office, thinking no one could match him.
idiomatic: He also trusted in rank and office, believing none could equal him.

literal: He told his son Shi, "Just let my son and me suffice to surpass others—there is no need to teach him painfully.
idiomatic: He told his son Shi, "Let my son and me alone surpass others—no need to drill him hard.

literal: " Toward his uncles and brothers he was like toward slaves; husband and wife sat and ate together while he made his uncles eat leftovers.
idiomatic: " He treated uncles and brothers like slaves; he and his wife ate together while making uncles take their leftovers.

literal: His arrogant lack of ritual was like this, and people of the time mocked him.
idiomatic: Contemporaries mocked him for such arrogant lack of ritual.

literal: In the eighth year of Zhenjun he died.
idiomatic: In the eighth year of Zhenjun he died — so the record runs.

literal: He was posthumously made Grand Commandant with posthumous title Wenzuan.
idiomatic: He was posthumously named grand commandant with the title Wenzuan.

literal: His son Pingguo inherited the title.
idiomatic: His son Pingguo succeeded.

literal: He married the Princess of Chengyang, was made Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law, Palace Attendant, and Director of the Secretariat, and became one of the crown prince's four tutors.
idiomatic: He married the Princess of Chengyang and became commandant of the imperial son-in-law, palace attendant, director of the secretariat, and one of the crown prince's four tutors.

literal: In the first year of Zhengping he died.
idiomatic: In the first year of Zhengping he died — so the record runs.

literal: His son Fugan inherited the title.
idiomatic: His son Fugan succeeded.

literal: He married the Princess of Jibei and was made Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law.
idiomatic: He married the Princess of Jibei and became commandant of the imperial son-in-law.

literal: In the second year of Heping he died.
idiomatic: In the second year of Heping he died — so the record runs.

literal: His posthumous title was Kang.
idiomatic: He received the posthumous title Kang.

literal: He had no son.
idiomatic: He left no son.

literal: Fugan's younger brother Pi inherited the title.
idiomatic: Fugan's younger brother Pi succeeded.

literal: He married the Princess of Xinping and was made Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law.
idiomatic: He married the Princess of Xinping and became commandant of the imperial son-in-law.

literal: He was also appointed garrison general of Hulao and repeatedly offended through unlawful conduct.
idiomatic: He was also made garrison general of Hulao and repeatedly broke the law.

literal: Emperor Gaozu, because he was of a house of old merit and virtue, reproved him and pardoned him.
idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu, remembering old service, rebuked him and pardoned him each time.

literal: He was transferred to be General Who Campaigns East and commander of the Tujing garrison.
idiomatic: He was made general who campaigns east and commander of the Tujing garrison.

literal: Pi rewarded good and punished evil and strove to discipline himself deeply.
idiomatic: Pi rewarded the good and punished the wicked and applied himself with strict self-discipline.

literal: At the time the Hu of Xihe rebelled; Pi wished to punish them, but the capital commandant of Lishi, Guo Luotou, resisted and would not obey.
idiomatic: When the Hu of Xihe rebelled, Pi wished to strike them, but Lishi commandant Guo Luotou refused to obey.

literal: Pi thereupon submitted a memorial impeaching himself, on the grounds that his authority could not restrain subordinates, and asked to undergo execution.
idiomatic: Pi memorialized to impeach himself, saying his authority could not restrain subordinates, and asked to suffer execution.

literal: Emperor Gaozu thereupon dismissed Luotou from office.
idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu dismissed Luotou from office.

literal: The mountain Hu Liu Shipo raided commanderies and counties; Pi attacked and destroyed them.
idiomatic: The mountain Hu Liu Shipo raided the commanderies; Pi destroyed them.

literal: From this time within his jurisdiction all was orderly, and none failed to respect and fear him.
idiomatic: From then on his district was orderly, and all respected and feared him.

literal: Later the Tujing garrison was changed to Fenzhou, and Pi was still appointed inspector.
idiomatic: When the Tujing garrison was reorganized as Fenzhou, Pi remained its governor.

literal: The former Tujing prefect Liu Sheng had great authority and kindness in the commandery; when his term ended and he returned to the capital, more than eight hundred Hu came to Pi to request him.
idiomatic: Former prefect Liu Sheng had ruled Tujing with authority and kindness; when his term ended and he returned to court, over eight hundred Hu petitioned Pi to bring him back.

literal: The former Dingyang magistrate Wu Pingren also had grace and trust; registered households increased severalfold.
idiomatic: Former Dingyang magistrate Wu Pingren likewise won trust, and registered households multiplied several times over.

literal: Because officials and people cherished them, Pi memorialized to request both.
idiomatic: Pi, seeing how officials and commoners cherished them, memorialized for both appointments.

literal: Emperor Gaozu approved all.
idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu granted each request.

literal: Since Pi had repeatedly recommended Sheng and the rest, the prefects and magistrates under his jurisdiction all sharpened themselves; awe and transformation spread widely, and the common people were at peace.
idiomatic: Pi's repeated recommendations of Sheng and others spurred every prefect and magistrate under him to sharpen their conduct, and his moral authority transformed the region.

literal: More than seven hundred men of the province, Li Gui and Guo Jizu among them, went to the palace gates to praise Pi's kindness and virtue.
idiomatic: Over seven hundred provincials, including Li Gui and Guo Jizu, went to the capital to praise Pi's kindness and virtue.

literal: Emperor Gaozu, because Pi's governance was sound and the people pleased, raised his rank and extended his term.
idiomatic: Seeing sound governance and a content populace, Emperor Gaozu raised Pi's rank and extended his term of office.

literal: Later he was summoned as Director of the Imperial Household.
idiomatic: He was later summoned to be director of the imperial household.

literal: According to precedent his princely title was reduced to Duke Who Founded the State of Weijun with a fief of five hundred households.
idiomatic: By precedent his title was reduced to Duke Who Founded the State of Weijun, fief five hundred households.

literal: He was again appointed General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Yan Province, garrisoning Guangning.
idiomatic: He was made general who pacifies the north and inspector of Yan, garrisoning Guangning.

literal: Soon he was transferred to be commander over all military affairs of Xia Province and the Gaoping garrison, with his existing rank, Inspector of Xia Province, garrisoning Tongwan.
idiomatic: Soon he was made commander of Xia Province and the Gaoping garrison, retained his existing rank, became inspector of Xia, and garrisoned Tongwan.

literal: He was again appointed Palace Attendant and Director of the Secretariat.
idiomatic: He was again made palace attendant and director of the secretariat.

literal: In Mu Tai's rebellion Pi had secretly communicated with him; after an amnesty the matter came out, and his enfeoffment was stripped—he became a registered commoner.
idiomatic: During Mu Tai's rebellion Pi had secretly communicated with the plotters; after an amnesty exposed the affair, his fief was revoked and he was reduced to common registration.

literal: He died at home.
idiomatic: He passed away at home.

literal: Under Emperor Shizong he was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Heng Province.
idiomatic: Under Emperor Shizong he was posthumously made general who pacifies the north and inspector of Heng.

literal: His son Jian, courtesy name Wanxing, was open and direct by nature and rather loved literature and history.
idiomatic: His son Jian, styled Wanxing, was frank by nature and fond of letters.

literal: He began his career as Secretary of the Palace and was gradually promoted to Direct-palace General and concurrent Defender of the Martial Guards.
idiomatic: He began as secretary of the palace, rose to direct-palace general, and served concurrently as defender of the martial guards.

literal: Jian's wife was Erzhu Rong's younger sister; Jian often relied on Rong.
idiomatic: Jian's wife was Erzhu Rong's sister; Jian often leaned on Rong.

literal: After Rong entered Luoyang he was appointed General Who Pacifies the East, Household Grandee with the Golden Seal and Purple Cord, General Who Campaigns North, and enfeoffed as Duke Who Founded the State of Jibei commandery.
idiomatic: After Rong entered Luoyang he was made general who pacifies the east, household grandee with the golden seal and purple cord, general who campaigns north, and duke who founded the state of Jibei commandery.

literal: Later he was transferred to Scattered Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Left Household Grandee, concurrent Master of Writing, Northern Route Mobile Headquarters, and affairs of Bing Province.
idiomatic: Later he became scattered cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, grand general of chariots and cavalry, left household grandee, concurrent master of writing, northern-route mobile headquarters, and overseer of Bing.

literal: When Yuan Ye was established, Jian was made concurrent Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing; soon he was transferred to Palace Attendant and Rapid Cavalry Grand General.
idiomatic: When Yuan Ye was enthroned, Jian was made concurrent right vice director of the masters of writing; soon he became palace attendant and rapid-cavalry grand general.

literal: At the end of Emperor Chu's reign he held his existing rank, Three Excellencies of Honor, and was Inspector of Luo Province.
idiomatic: At the end of Emperor Chu's reign he held his existing rank, three excellencies of honor, and was inspector of Luo.

literal: In the Tianping era, for an offense he killed himself north of the city of Wuyuan.
idiomatic: In the Tianping era he took his own life north of Wuyuan for an offense.

literal: His son Qianya, in the Wuding era, was libationer of the Bureau that Opens Offices.
idiomatic: His son Qianya, in the Wuding era, was libationer of the bureau that opens offices.

literal: Jian's younger brother Yan, courtesy name Jinxing.
idiomatic: Jian's younger brother Yan, styled Jinxing.

literal: Upon leaving the russet he was made Outer Palace Attendant, enfeoffed as Baron Who Founded the State of Xinxing county, and gradually promoted to Direct-palace Regular Attendant in charge of Yun Province affairs.
idiomatic: Upon leaving the russet he was made outer palace attendant, enfeoffed baron who founded the state of Xinxing county, and rose to direct-palace regular attendant in charge of Yun.

literal: Pi's younger brother Liang, courtesy name Youfu, at first styled Laosheng, early showed bearing and style.
idiomatic: Pi's younger brother Liang, styled Youfu, first styled Laosheng, showed refinement and presence from youth.

literal: Under Emperor Xianzu he first entered service as Attendant Censor.
idiomatic: Under Emperor Xianzu he began his career as attendant censor.

literal: He married the Princess of Zhongshan, was appointed Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law, enfeoffed as Prince of Zhao commandery, and given the additional posts Palace Attendant and General Who Campaigns South.
idiomatic: He married the Princess of Zhongshan, became commandant of the imperial son-in-law, was enfeoffed prince of Zhao commandery, and named palace attendant and general who campaigns south.

literal: His fief was changed to Prince of Changle.
idiomatic: His fief was transferred to the princedom of Changle.

literal: At the beginning of Emperor Gaozu's reign he was appointed Bearer of the Staff, Inspector of Qin Province.
idiomatic: At Gaozu's accession he was made bearer of the staff and inspector of Qin.

literal: Within the province, before his term was complete, he won great renown.
idiomatic: Before his term ended he won great renown in the province.

literal: He was summoned as Master of Writing Within the Hall.
idiomatic: He was summoned as master of writing within the hall.

literal: He was again transferred to Bearer of the Staff, General Who Campaigns West, Colonel Protector of the Western Rong, and Grand General of the Dunhuang Garrison.
idiomatic: He was made bearer of the staff, general who campaigns west, colonel protector of the western rong, and grand general of the Dunhuang garrison.

literal: His government favored leniency and simplicity; he relieved and supported the exhausted.
idiomatic: His rule favored leniency and simplicity; he relieved the poor and exhausted.

literal: When he was summoned back to court the common people missed him.
idiomatic: When he was recalled to court the people missed him.

literal: He was appointed commander over all military affairs of Qin, Liang, and Yi provinces, General Who Campaigns South, concurrent Colonel Protector of the Western Rong, and commander of the Chouchi garrison.
idiomatic: He was made commander of Qin, Liang, and Yi, general who campaigns south, colonel protector of the western rong, and commander of the Chouchi garrison.

literal: At the time the King of Dangchang, Liang Miji, died; his son Mibo succeeded, was pressed by Tuyuhun, and came to flee to Chouchi.
idiomatic: Dangchang king Liang Miji died, and his son Mibo succeeded; harried by Tuyuhun, Mibo fled to Chouchi for refuge.

literal: Liang considered that Miji's long-standing submission to the frontier was well known,[2] and pitied his destruction;
idiomatic: Liang judged that Miji's long submission to the court was well known,[2] and pitied his fall;

literal: Mibo was violent and perverse, abandoned by the Di and Qiang;
idiomatic: Mibo was violent and perverse and abandoned by the Di and Qiang tribes;

literal: Miji's elder brother's son Micheng, whom the tribal peoples gladly followed, memorialized asking to receive him.
idiomatic: Miji's nephew Micheng, whom the tribes gladly followed, memorialized asking that he be installed instead.

literal: Emperor Gaozu approved.
idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu agreed.

literal: Thereupon he led thirty thousand horsemen, halted at Longhu, routed Tuyuhun, installed Micheng, and returned.
idiomatic: He then led thirty thousand horse, halted at Longhu, drove off Tuyuhun, installed Micheng, and withdrew.

literal: At that time the Qiang of Jieling Bigu, Dong Gengnu and Si Bei among them, led a multitude of several thousand men, raided Chouchi, and encamped at Yangxia Ridge; Liang's deputy Yang Lingzhen led horsemen and attacked and drove them off.
idiomatic: Then the Jieling Bigu Qiang, Dong Gengnu and Si Bei among them, led several thousand men against Chouchi and encamped at Yangxia Ridge; Liang's deputy Yang Lingzhen drove them off.

literal: The Di chieftain Yang Bu, since Yanxing, had followed the army in campaigns through twenty-one battles; former garrison commanders had suppressed him and never reported his merit.
idiomatic: The Di chieftain Yang Bu had fought in twenty-one campaigns since Yanxing, yet successive garrison commanders had suppressed his record and never reported his merit.

literal: Liang memorialized to make Bu Grand Warden of Guangye; the powerful families were all pleased, and within the borders there was great peace.
idiomatic: Liang memorialized to appoint Bu grand warden of Guangye; local magnates were pleased and the region knew great peace.

literal: He was summoned as Palace Attendant and Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: He was summoned to be palace attendant and right vice director of the masters of writing.

literal: [3] At that time Sizhou was re-established.
idiomatic: [3] At that time Sizhou was re-established — so the record runs.

literal: Emperor Gaozu said, "Sizhou has just been founded and has no staff officers; a Rectifier must be appointed to fix selections.
idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu said, "Sizhou has only just been founded and lacks staff; we must appoint a Rectifier to govern selection.

literal: Yet the Rectifier's post requires both virtue and renown.
idiomatic: That office demands both virtue and public standing.

literal: Under Emperor Shizu, Cui Hao was Rectifier of Jizhou and Changsun Song Rectifier of Sizhou—truly men well chosen.
idiomatic: Under Emperor Shizu, Cui Hao was Rectifier of Jizhou and Changsun Song Rectifier of Sizhou—true examples of the right choice.

literal: You ministers and grandees should deliberate and recommend among yourselves; it must be fitting.
idiomatic: You ministers should deliberate and recommend with care.

literal: " Director of the Masters of Writing Lu Rui recommended Liang as Grand Rectifier of Sizhou.
idiomatic: " Director Lu Rui recommended Liang as grand rectifier of Sizhou.
